ai.description: This 25–30 mm frog is brown with a dark lateral band. It features a pointed snout and elongated, slender digits. Males display a unique foot-flagging behavior during breeding.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus kottigeharensis* is best distinguished by the distinct, pale-colored longitudinal stripe running along the center of its back, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus kottigeharensis* inhabits rocky, fast-flowing streams within evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, male *Micrixalus kottigeharensis* perform "foot-flagging" displays, extending their hind limbs to signal to rivals and potential mates near streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus kottigeharensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in subterranean nests within stream beds, which the males actively guard.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus kottigeharensis* is endemic to the central Western Ghats in the Indian state of Karnataka, typically inhabiting streams at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kottigehar Bubble-nest Frog emits a high-pitched, metallic "tink" sound repeated in rapid, rhythmic pulses while calling from rocky, fast-flowing forest streams.
